strongest_angle: Analysis of Renfe's emergency safety directive following the Urda high-speed rail collision, detailing the mandate for trains to halt and proceed under a 40 km/h visual supervision limit after signaling failures.

key_facts.fact: Renfe has introduced a new safety directive for high speed operations, requiring trains to halt and proceed at a maximum speed of 40 km/h under visual supervision after cab signalling failures following the fatal Urda collision that killed at least 69 people.
The fatal accident occurred in Urda, Toledo, representing the second high-speed railway tragedy in Spain in nine months on the Madrid-Sevilla line.
Renfe launched the new operational conditions and mandatory instructions for train drivers on the Madrid-Sevilla high-speed rail line to prevent new accidents following the disaster.
